item.title: Judge upholds disqualification of acting U.S. attorney Sarcone in New York
item.description: U.S. District Judge Lorna Schofield denied the federal government's request to pause a ruling that disqualified acting federal prosecutor John Sarcone III and blocked his subpoenas against New York Attorney General Letitia James, ruling that Sarcone had no legal authority to serve as acting U.S. attorney for the Northern District of New York.

item.title: NJ driver shuts off lights in So. Herkimer County after accident
item.description: A New Jersey driver and his two passengers were hospitalized after he crashed into a power pole, sending power lines down across the Thruway on Wednesday and putting several towns in Southern Herkimer County in the dark.

item.title: NYS burn ban starts Monday, March 16
item.description: New York State has implemented its annual spring burn ban from March 16 to May 14 to reduce the risk of wildfires, with violators facing fines of at least $500, and certain exemptions for farms and residents in towns with populations under 20,000.

item.title: Assembly and Senate proposed income tax changes
item.description: There were proposed personal income tax changes in the legislative budget proposals. On Thursday, with both houses in session, Assemblymembers, in particular, were in debate about raising personal income taxes.

item.title: Majority of New Yorkers forced to choose between groceries and bare necessities: poll
item.description: A poll released by No Kid Hungry found that 74% of families with kids in New York have to choose between food and other necessities, with 87% of Black and 84% of Latino families disproportionately affected, and 52% of respondents taking on additional debt to afford meals.
